extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, patent examiners, judges, and law students
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and doctrinal rules for assessing novelty (anticipation) of patents under U.S. law: what prior patents, publications, uses, models, applications, experiments, and other events will or will not negate novelty of a claimed invention. Includes special rules for designs, combinations, abandoned applications, drawings/models, and date-of-invention issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-inventor requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant must be the first inventor of the invention covered by his application at the time of making his application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant learned of a prior disclosure before his date of conception he would not be the inventor; prior foreign knowledge known to others in this country (but not known to the applicant before conception) does not negate novelty in the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of later-issued U.S. patents and certain foreign patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty is not negatived by any United States patent which was issued after the contested invention was made (even if applied for before that event), nor by any prior private patent granted in a foreign country, nor by a public patent granted in England unless the latter was sealed before the person obtaining the American patent made the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain foreign patents (e.g., a French patent) become effective to negative novelty when sealed and enrolled; German patents are dated by publication ('ausgegeben').

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent applications as prior art (when they can anticipate)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior application filed in the Patent Office before the contested invention may negative novelty if the prior art is shown in the specification or drawing of that application and there had been some actual use of the invention before the contested invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mere application, by itself, is not of itself a part of the prior art and, generally, cannot be used to anticipate another patent unless it both (1) was filed before the later inventor's invention and (2) its specification/drawings show the relevant prior art and there was prior actual use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full description in prior patent/publication negates novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: A full description in the specification of a prior public patent (or a printed publication) of the subject covered by a later patent negates novelty even though the earlier patent did not claim that subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings in prior patents/publications that unmistakably disclose the invention can likewise anticipate; nothing can be used to contradict the face of a patent except what's on its face.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed publication as prior art and its scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A printed publication is anything printed and, without secrecy, distributed to any part of the public in any country; such a publication may negative novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exposure of printed matter for sale can suffice; mere existence is not enough (except deposit in a public library). Drawings in publications, if their meaning is undeniable, may anticipate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement requirement for anticipation
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior patent or printed publication will not negative novelty unless the information contained therein is full enough and precise enough to enable a person skilled in the art to perform the process or make the thing covered by the later patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testimony is not admissible to alter the meaning of the prior patent's face; expert testimony on meaning must be supported by reasoning to be weighty. A prior patent need not have been reduced to practice to anticipate if it embodies the elements and discloses the principle of operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skillful mechanic doctrine (minor omissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A mere omission of something which a skillful mechanic would supply is not fatal to anticipation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'skillful mechanic' is one able to vary form without varying substance; it does not include mere servile imitators. Prior patents that embody elements and the principle of operation can anticipate even if devices would be incapable of successful operation without routine adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophetic statements/surmises insufficient to anticipate
rubrics_metrics.description: Prophetical suggestions and surmises in prior patents or publications as to what results may be achieved are not enough to negative the novelty of a later patent that actually accomplishes that result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speculative or predictive statements that do not disclose a working, enabling teaching will not anticipate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation of an article of manufacture by description alone
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim for an article of manufacture may be anticipated by a prior patent or printed publication that describes the article even without describing any process of making it, provided knowledge of the article would teach a skillful mechanic some process of making it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a skilled artisan could infer how to make the article from the description, the prior description can be an anticipation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of abandoned patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandoned applications for patents do not, by the statutes, operate as bars to patents to later applicants and do not generally negative novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abandoned applications are usually only written representations and not published by the Patent Office; certified copies published later operate from their own publication date. If there is evidence the applicant attempted to carry the invention into practical use, the abandoned application may be admissible to help determine date and nature of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of successful application documents distinct from issued patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty is not negatived by any successful application for a patent, nor by documents pertaining thereto that differ from the letters patent issued in pursuance thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such applications/documents can, however, be used to prove the date of the invention set forth therein.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpublished drawings and private models do not negate novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty of a machine or manufacture is not negatived by any prior unpublished drawings, no matter how completely they exhibit the patented invention, nor by any prior model, however fully it may coincide with the patented thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory language and public-policy reasons (seclusion, misunderstanding, temptation to perjury) justify excluding private/unpublished drawings and models as prior art. 'Model' here means a pattern or reduced-scale representation, not an operative structure identical to the patented structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial identity required to negate novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty is not negatived by anything not substantially identical with the subject of the patent, even though the function of the prior thing was identical with that of the patented matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A valid patent may be granted for a new means of producing an old result. If the patented thing possesses distinct and apparently important characteristics not possessed by the alleged anticipation, novelty is preserved. However, a prior thing that includes the subject of the patent among other elements may still defeat novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary vs. secondary patent distinction (anticipation vs infringement)
rubrics_metrics.description: That which would infringe if later may not necessarily anticipate if earlier — the distinction between primary patents and secondary patents matters for whether earlier art anticipates or only limits invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A contrivance that would infringe a primary patent if later might not anticipate that patent if earlier; the earlier device may only relegate a patent to a secondary position rather than fully negate novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of unsuccessful or abandoned experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: An unsuccessful abandoned experimental machine or manufacture may possibly negative the novelty of a later invention, but not necessarily; whether it does depends on identity and evidence of operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the earlier thing was identical and used long enough to show it would work, it may negate novelty. If unsuccessful due to faults of principle, that shows substantial difference; if unsuccessful due to weak construction, it may still negate novelty. Courts should not be required to decipher anticipations in unfinished work and surmises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent novelty standard (ordinary observer test)
rubrics_metrics.description: The novelty of a design is determined by comparative appearance of that design and prior designs in the eyes of average observers, not by analytical inspection by experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A design is not necessarily negated by collecting its features from scattered prior designs; visual impression on ordinary observers controls novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior similar items incapable of function do not negate novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty is not negatived by anything beneficially incapable of the function of the patented subject, even though apparently similar thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior device was theoretically similar but practically of no value for the intended function, it may not negate novelty (examples: differing syringe constructions, materials that make a composition unsuitable for the intended use).

rubrics_metrics.name: New combination of old parts preserves novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty is not negatived by antiquity of parts; a new assemblage or combination of old elements can be novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the new assemblage is merely aggregation with no new mode of operation, it may lack invention (patentable inventive step) but still be novel relative to prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accidental prior occurrences and understood prior use
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty is not negatived by a prior accidental occurrence or production whose character and function were not recognized until after the date of the later invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, novelty can be negated by proof of prior use where that use was understood in point of method even if not correctly understood as to result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal rule: anticipating event must precede the date of invention (and same-inventor rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: An anticipating event (invention, patent, publication, patent grant) only negatives novelty if it occurred prior to the date of the invention secured by the later patent; where two patents for the same invention are granted to the same inventor, the later is void because dates of invention are the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When several patents are granted to one inventor on different inventions in the same art, application dates (in the absence of evidence of dates of making) determine relative rank. The rule that the first application is taken to represent first invention is subject to evidence of identical invention dates among patents to the same inventor.
